title: Clock Card Matcher
description: Set the Earth's turn beside a day, change long lengths of time a step at a time, match clock cards with the time passed after 12 o'clock, and write an end time on the 24-hour clock.
modes: none. One flow, one phase at a time. The host mounts a phase (phase prop). With navigableDots true, or no phase, the child may jump phases with the dots (user mode); otherwise the dots show progress and the teacher agent drives window.toolApi (AI mode). The last phase, and a whole lesson, end on the summary page, where Free play and Play again sit. With navDots the dots are controls in AI mode too: a tap on a dot starts that phase.

stage.sizing: the frame is min(100vw, 177.78vh) wide and min(100vh, 56.25vw) tall (dvh where supported); the svg fills it. Nothing scrolls.

bands.header: 0 to 80. One line: the tool name, a measured dot, the phase concept; Hint, sound and restart as round controls far right.
bands.canvas: 92 to 640. One rounded card holding the key at its top right (Answer, Close, Enter, Next, or the Yes / No keys; no question bar), the working area (the whole card until Answer is tapped) and the answer drawer that slides in from the right; the summary page covers it at the end.
bands.footer: 652 to 900. The mascot at the far left on its ground line, the speech bubble beside it (y 656 to 892, the question and every line, printed), one small dot per phase at the right.

zones.layout: board, key only: no question bar, only its key at the right end of the top row (the question is on the bubble); the working area is the whole card (64, 108, 1472 x 520) until the child taps Answer, when the answer drawer (as tall as the working area, the key on its top row reading Close) slides in from the right
zones.controls: circles r 28 at cx 1388, 1460, 1532, cy 40: Hint (data-control again), sound, restart; 72-unit finger boxes
zones.dots: one small dot per phase at the footer's right (72-unit finger boxes, centred on the bubble), no text; in user AND AI mode each is a button (data-control phase-dot, data-phase k) that starts its phase

stage.noSidebar: There is no sidebar. The canvas takes every unit the chrome can spare.
stage.noScoreBox: There is no score box on the stage. The score leaves on finished and onComplete and is shown once, as stars on the summary page.

writeup.why: Keep 1 day as 24 h beside the Earth's turn, change long lengths of time a step at a time, match a clock card with the time passed after 12 o'clock, and give an end time on the 24-hour clock.
writeup.look: A day bar with the Earth's turn beside it, a ladder for long lengths of time, sixteen face down cards, a time line with jumps, and a tray of six word cards.
writeup.stage: Three bands across 1600 by 900. The header runs 0 to 80 and is one line only: 'Clock Card Matcher' in ink at the far left, a small dot set clear of the name, the phase title beside the dot on the same line, the host's navigation, and sound and restart as three round controls at the far right. The canvas runs 92 to 746, one rounded card on the paper colour. At its top left, at x 64, y 108 and 330 by 76, sits the running count: the number of pairs matched. It is never a score. The working area is 1086 by 528 at x 64, y 202. The day bar fills the top of the area along y 230 from x 90 to x 1000, one whole day long, with the Earth's turn drawn beside it along y 320 as a bar a little shorter. The tray of six word cards, second, minute, hour, a.m., p.m. and calendar, stands along y 420, and each turns over to its meaning. On the second phase the ladder of days, hours and minutes stands at x 90, y 250 with the long length of time in deep blue, labelled Given, and the working is written in ink beside it. On the third phase sixteen cards lie face down in two rows of eight along y 260 and y 470, each 110 by 170. A clock card is a round clock face with twelve numbers, its hour hand and minute hand near-black ink and its hour hand moved on from its number for the minutes. A time card is the time passed after 12 o'clock, in minutes alone or in seconds alone. Two cards are turned at a time, and a pair that matches stays face up in green, labelled Answer. On the fourth phase the time line with the start and the length of time in deep blue runs along y 400, the jumps in violet, labelled Jump, and the end time is written on the 24-hour clock in green, labelled Answer, at x 120, y 650. The row of five can-dos stands at x 850, y 660, and each is ticked as it is met. Down the right of the canvas, in the same rectangle on every phase and never animated in or out, the question sits above the answer slot at x 1186, y 250 (356 by 92) that holds what the child has given, and under it the pad at x 1170, y 368 (388 by 363). The pad is ten number keys with a delete key, and keys for days, h, min and s. The footer runs 758 to 900: the voice caption at the far left with its speaking dot beside it, measuring its own wrap and dropping a type size rather than spilling, and the phase bar at the right with the question count under it. There is no sidebar and no score box anywhere, and nothing is ever written over the working area. Content colours are the chapter's own, and the nine tools of this chapter share them. What the question gives, as a clock time, a length of time, a start date or a number of days, is deep blue, labelled Given or Start. What the working reaches, as an end time, a length of time, a converted time or a date, is green, labelled Answer, End or How long. The thin second hand and the seconds it counts are vermilion, labelled Second hand. One jump along a time line, and one regrouped unit carried or borrowed, are violet, labelled Jump, Carry or Regroup. On a day bar the half from noon until just before midnight is rose, labelled p.m., and the half from midnight until just before noon stays warm white inside its outline, labelled a.m. The hand, digit, column, jump or date being worked on now is amber. Grey is kept for a zero holding a place open, labelled Place holder, and for nothing else. The hour hand and the minute hand, dials, tick marks, time lines, arrows, operation signs and step labels are near-black ink, and anything dimmed fades to half strength. Chrome never borrows one of the content colours, and each reading survives with the colour taken away, because a part is told by its written label before it is told by its colour.
writeup.finish: The matched pairs stay face up on the stage with the last end time beside them in green, and the row of five can-dos stays as the child ticked it.

phases.win: the gap is seen and the words a little less than a day light up
phases.does: drags the Earth's turn bar beside the day bar and sees the small gap between them
phases.goal: the Earth turns once round in about 23 h 56 min, a little less than a day. 1 day is still 24 h
phases.says: Are the two bars exactly the same? Which one is a little shorter?
phases.check: Away from the screen: is the Earth's turn a little more or a little less than a day?
phases.feels: the two bars side by side with a small gap between them
phases.hands: Lay a strip of paper as long as a day on a desk. Lay a strip that is a little shorter beside it and say which is which. Then look at a clock and say how many hours make a day.
phases.tries: First rung: drag the Earth's turn bar beside the day bar. Second rung: find the gap between the ends. Third rung: say the two facts together, before the question's own wording returns.

wrong.why: a day is how long it feels the turn takes
wrong.move: says the Earth's turn is exactly one day
wrong.screen: the two bars stay side by side, the gap between their ends lights amber, and the words a little less than a day are written in ink under the shorter bar

wrong.why: two bars of different lengths look as if one of them must be wrong
wrong.move: makes a clock day shorter than 24 h to match the Earth's turn
wrong.screen: the day bar stays at its full length, marked 1 day, which is 24 h, and the Earth's turn bar is drawn beside it, shorter and lit amber

phases.screen: a day bar for 1 day, which is 24 h, with a slightly shorter bar for the Earth's turn beside it
phases.soWhat: the Earth turns once round in about 23 h 56 min, a little less than a day. 1 day is still 24 h

phases.win: the minutes turn green with the working written beneath
phases.does: breaks the days into hours and then the hours into minutes, adding the leftover part at each step, and adds or takes apart two long lengths
phases.goal: long lengths of time are changed a step at a time, days to hours by multiplying by 24 and then hours to minutes by multiplying by 60
phases.says: One step at a time. Which unit comes next?
phases.check: Away from the screen: to change days to minutes, which unit do you go through?
phases.feels: two steps down the ladder, the second bigger than the first
phases.hands: Write a long length in days and hours on a card. Change the days to hours first on paper and add the leftover hours, then change the hours to minutes, saying each unit fact aloud.
phases.tries: First rung: change a few days to hours. Second rung: change those hours to minutes. Third rung: the same task with a leftover part of hours, before the question's own length returns.

wrong.why: days and minutes are the two ends of the ladder, and the step between them looks small
wrong.move: multiplies the days by sixty straight away
wrong.screen: the hours rung is lit amber between them, and the days are broken into hour bars first, while the child's number stays in the slot

wrong.why: the first step looks like the whole job
wrong.move: changes the days to hours but stops there when the question asks for minutes
wrong.screen: the hour bars stay, the minutes rung is lit amber below them, and each hour bar waits to be broken into sixty minute bars

phases.screen: a ladder of days, hours and minutes with a long length of time set in deep blue
phases.soWhat: long lengths of time are changed a step at a time, days to hours by multiplying by 24, then hours to minutes by multiplying by 60, with the leftover part added at each step

phases.win: the matched pair stays face up and turns green
phases.does: turns two cards at a time, reads a clock card as hours and minutes after 12 o'clock, changes that to minutes or seconds, and keeps a pair that matches
phases.goal: a clock card is matched with the time passed after 12 o'clock, written in minutes or in seconds, and every hour hand has moved on for the minutes
phases.says: Turn two cards. Do the hours and minutes match the time card?
phases.check: Away from the screen: when the hands show a quarter past a number, is the hour hand on the number or a little past it?
phases.feels: a matched pair staying face up and turning green
phases.hands: Draw eight clock faces on cards and, on eight more, write the time passed after 12 o'clock in minutes or in seconds. Turn them all face down, turn two at a time, and keep a pair only when the hands and the time agree.
phases.tries: First rung: turn just one clock card and read its time. Second rung: turn a time card and match it. Third rung: the same task with the whole set of cards, before the question's own cards return.

wrong.why: the hour hand is short and easy to read, so it looks like the whole time
wrong.move: matches a clock card with a time card by its hour alone
wrong.screen: the two cards turn face down again, the minute hand on the clock card is lit amber, and the minutes it counts are added in ink to the hours

wrong.why: the hour hand looks as if it points at the number just ahead of it
wrong.move: reads the hour hand as if it were still on its number
wrong.screen: the hour hand is drawn again at its true place, moved on for the minutes, with the small step it has taken lit amber

wrong.why: a time card is only a number, and its unit is the small word after it
wrong.move: matches a card in minutes with a card in seconds
wrong.screen: the two cards stay face up, the unit word on the time card is lit amber, and the clock card is read again in that unit

phases.screen: sixteen cards face down in two rows of eight, eight clock cards and eight time cards
phases.soWhat: a clock card is matched with the time passed after 12 o'clock, written in minutes alone or in seconds alone, and every hour hand has moved on for the minutes

phases.win: the end time turns green in four digits and the word hours
phases.does: jumps the whole hours and then the minutes, reads the 12-hour end time, and writes it on the 24-hour clock
phases.goal: an end time is found by jumping from the start and is written on the 24-hour clock as four digits and the word hours
phases.says: Jump the hours, then the minutes. Now write it on the twenty-four hour clock.
phases.check: Away from the screen: 20 min after a time in the afternoon, how do you write it on the 24-hour clock?
phases.feels: the end time turning green in four digits and the word hours
phases.hands: Write a start time on a paper time line, and cut two paper jumps for the hours and the minutes of a length of time. Lay them end to end, read the end time on the 12-hour clock, and then write it on the 24-hour clock.
phases.tries: First rung: jump the whole hours and read the time on the 12-hour clock. Second rung: jump the minutes as well. Third rung: the same task with an end time in the evening, before the question's own start returns.

wrong.why: the jump ends on a 12-hour time, and that time looks like the answer
wrong.move: gives the end time on the 12-hour clock when the question asks for the 24-hour clock
wrong.screen: the end time stays, and the four-digit form is lit amber beside it, waiting for its digits

wrong.why: the hour and the minutes look right on their own
wrong.move: writes an afternoon end time with the hour of the 12-hour clock and no 12 added
wrong.screen: the marker is drawn in the rose half, the tile of 12 h is lit amber, and the digits are written again with the tile on

phases.screen: a time line with a start and a length of time set in deep blue, and the 24-hour clock waiting
phases.soWhat: an end time is found by jumping from the start, and is written on the 24-hour clock as four digits and the word hours
phases.concept: An end time on the 24-hour clock

writeup.delight: On the third phase, when the last pair is matched, all sixteen cards flip face up together and the eight clock faces tick round to their times one after another.
writeup.opening: Every mount comes up already furnished for its phase with nothing yet matched. On the first phase a day bar for 1 day lies across the top with a slightly shorter bar for the Earth's turn beside it, and the tray of six word cards below. On the second the ladder of days, hours and minutes holds a long length of time in deep blue. On the third sixteen cards lie face down in two rows of eight. On the fourth a time line holds a start and a length of time in deep blue with the 24-hour clock waiting beside it. One thing moves, once: the shorter bar, the first card or the time line gives one slow pulse while the voice speaks its opening line.
writeup.freePlay: Any clock card set and matched, any length of time changed on the ladder, and any end time jumped and written on both clocks. Nothing to get right, no target and no timer. The child is left with the same stage and every control unlocked.
writeup.practice: Eight items over the four phases, easy first, on the Earth's turn, long lengths of time, clock cards and time cards, and an end time on the 24-hour clock.
voiceLines: A day, a ladder of time and sixteen cards face down.
Are the two bars exactly the same? Which one is a little shorter?
One step at a time. Which unit comes next?
Turn two cards. Do the hours and minutes match the time card?
Jump the hours, then the minutes. Now write it on the twenty-four hour clock.
A new round. Play it the same way.
Free play. Turn any cards and set any time.
Look at the cards again. Do the hands and the time agree?
You matched clock cards, changed long lengths of time and wrote an end time.

observations.why: the Earth turns once round in about 23 h 56 min, a little less than a day.
observations.soWhat: a clock still counts 1 day as 24 h, so both facts are true.
observations.observe: The bar for the Earth's turn was a little shorter than the day bar.

observations.why: each step down the ladder is a multiplication, and days and minutes are two steps apart.
observations.soWhat: change a long length of time one step at a time, and add the leftover part at each step.
observations.observe: The days were changed to hours before the hours were changed to minutes.

observations.why: the hour hand moves on as the minutes pass.
observations.soWhat: a clock card is matched with the time passed after 12 o'clock, in minutes alone or in seconds alone.
observations.observe: Every hour hand on a clock card had moved on from its number.

observations.why: the 24-hour clock writes the hours and minutes after midnight in four digits.
observations.soWhat: an end time is jumped from the start and then written on the 24-hour clock.
observations.observe: The end time turned into four digits and the word hours.

phases.screen: a day bar for 1 day, which is 24 h, with a slightly shorter bar for the Earth's turn beside it
phases.win: the gap is seen and the words a little less than a day light up
phases.traceback: the Earth's bar lies under the day bar, the last hour is drawn large with its 4 min gap lit amber, then 23 h 56 min and less than a day are written; for the hours, every hour box is numbered
ladder: Look at where the Earth's bar ends.
Count the hour boxes on the day bar.
Which bar ends first, the day or the Earth's turn?
Do the two bars end together in the last hour?
Count the minutes between the two ends in the last hour.

phases.screen: a ladder of days, hours and minutes with a long length of time set in deep blue
phases.win: the minutes turn green with the working written beneath
phases.traceback: the hours rung lights amber and the days are changed to hours with the working written beside it, then the hours to minutes, ending on the answer in green
ladder: Go down the ladder one rung at a time.
Each day on the ladder is worth 24 h.
A year has 365 days of 24 h each.
2 days are 2 × 24 hours, then add the 3 h.
Multiply all those hours by 60 to get minutes.

phases.screen: sixteen cards face down in two rows of eight, eight clock cards and eight time cards
phases.win: the matched pair stays face up and turns green
phases.traceback: the minute hand lights amber and the hour hand's step past its number is drawn, then the hours are changed to minutes and the minutes added, ending on the time card in green
ladder: Read the hours, then the minutes on the clock.
Which number has the short hand just passed?
Seconds are asked for this time, not minutes.
Count 60 min for each whole hour the short hand has passed.
Then add the minutes the long hand shows.

phases.screen: a time line with a start and a length of time set in deep blue, and the 24-hour clock waiting
phases.win: the end time turns green in four digits and the word hours
phases.traceback: the jumps are drawn to the 12-hour end time, which lights amber, the hour has 12 added to it, and the end time is written green in four digits and the word hours
ladder: Write four digits, and after noon add 12 to the hour.
The 24-hour clock goes on counting past 12 after noon.
Four digits again: is the end time after noon?
Is the end in the part marked a.m., or p.m.?
After noon, the 24-hour hour is 12 more than the hour on the line.

items.win: Yes, 4 min short of a day is about 23 h 56 min.

ladder: One half of the day bar has 12 boxes.
Add the boxes of both halves of the day.
items.win: Yes, a clock day has 24 h.

ladder: Look at the gap in the last hour.
Which bar would need 4 more minutes to reach the end?
items.win: Yes, the Earth's turn is a little less than a day.

ladder: Find 10 groups of 24 h.
Multiplying by 10 puts a zero after the number.
Find 365 × 24, one part at a time.
Work out 365 × 20 and 365 × 4, then add.
items.win: Yes, a year of 365 days is 8,760 h.

ladder: Each hour the short hand has passed is 60 min.
Add on the minutes the long hand points to.
Minutes first, then change them to seconds.
Each minute is 60 s, so multiply the minutes by 60.
Find 3:15 on the line: which part is it in?
Add 12 to an afternoon hour, then write the minutes.

items.win: Yes, the lamp goes off at 1335 hours.

onWrong.marks: Nothing is marked, no colour means good or bad. The miss empties the answer slot at once (every digit, every box, a picked choice), so it is empty through the traceback; the pad re-opens empty after it.
tracebacks: Phase 1: the Earth's bar lies under the day bar, the last hour is drawn large with its 4 min gap lit amber, then 23 h 56 min and less than a day are written; for the hours, every hour box is numbered
Phase 2: the hours rung lights amber and the days are changed to hours with the working written beside it, then the hours to minutes, ending on the answer in green
Phase 3: the minute hand lights amber and the hour hand's step past its number is drawn, then the hours are changed to minutes and the minutes added, ending on the time card in green
Phase 4: the jumps are drawn to the 12-hour end time, which lights amber, the hour has 12 added to it, and the end time is written green in four digits and the word hours

voice.opening: A day, a ladder of time and sixteen cards face down.
voice.onFreePlay: Free play. Turn any two cards and find the pairs.
voice.onMiss: the item's own miss line, then the phase's two ladder rungs, shown at once UNDER the pinned instruction and kept until the child acts again
voice.onFinish: You matched clock cards, changed long lengths of time and wrote an end time.
voice.rules: Silent: nothing is spoken (no device speech, no recorded clips, no Tap to start cover). The speech bubble is the guide: every instruction and hint is one printed page, numbers as words. The lesson is action-driven in every mode: a guide step's instruction stays until the child does the act it names; a wrong act shows that step's hint under the pinned instruction, a wrong answer the next rung of its ladder, and the hint stays unchanged until the child acts again; a right answer's next question, a phase's next phase and the summary's rows follow by themselves after a short celebration. The header's Hint key shows the step's hint or the next rung on demand. What is heard is sound effects (Web Audio), switched by the sound button, on in every mode. In classroom mode nothing waits for a tap except the pieces of a long line (the blinking arrow; a tap, Enter, Space, ArrowRight or PageDown on the bubble shows the next piece), and a tap on the bubble when nothing waits is the teacher's skip.

guide.playsOn: guide steps on phase 1, 2, 3, 4: the phase opens on its first instruction and waits for the child's act (getState guideStep, guideSteps, guideOn); the agent's check() performs the current step; the last act opens the first question. Other phases open on their printed teach lines, and a demo phase waits for the child's own act.

palette.rule: A content colour fills countable things only and chrome never borrows one; coloured numerals and words take a deeper ink of their colour (4.5:1).

toolQuestions.source: props.questions ?? props.additionalProps?.questions is read; the authored rows below keep their stage (fitHost returns null).

items.planQuestion: A pupil says the Earth turns once round in exactly 1 day. What is the better thing to say?

question.en: A pupil says the Earth turns in exactly 1 day; what is better to say?

items.planAnswer: The Earth turns once round in about 23 h 56 min, a little less than a day. A clock still counts 1 day as 24 h.

items.planQuestion: How many hours make 1 day on a clock?

question.en: How many hours make 1 day on a clock?

items.planQuestion: Is the Earth's turn a little more or a little less than 1 day?

question.en: Is the Earth's turn a little more or a little less than 1 day?

items.planAnswer: A little less: it takes about 23 h 56 min, a little less than a day

items.planQuestion: How many minutes are there in 2 days 3 h?

question.en: How many minutes are there in 2 days 3 h?

items.planQuestion: How many hours are there in 10 days?

question.en: How many hours are there in 10 days?

items.planQuestion: How many hours are there in a year of 365 days?

question.en: How many hours are there in a year of 365 days?

items.planQuestion: A clock card shows 25 min past 6. Which time card matches it, in minutes after 12 o'clock?

question.en: Turn the card with the ring; how many minutes after 12 o'clock is it?

items.planQuestion: A clock card shows 5 min past 2. Which time card, in minutes, matches it?

question.en: What does the next card with the ring show, in minutes?

items.planQuestion: A clock card shows 35 min past 2. Which time card, in seconds, matches it?

question.en: Turn the last card with the ring and change its time into seconds.

items.planAnswer: 9300 s, because 2 h 35 min is 155 min and 155 x 60 = 9300

items.planQuestion: A machine starts at 5:35 a.m. and runs for 7 h 40 min. When does it stop, on the 24-hour clock?

question.en: A machine runs 7 h 40 min from 5:35 a.m.; what is its 24-hour stop time?
On the 24-hour clock, how do you write 3:15 p.m.?

items.planQuestion: A lamp is switched on at 8:45 a.m. and stays on for 4 h 50 min. When does it go off, on the 24-hour clock?

question.en: A lamp lit at 8:45 a.m., stays on 4 h 50 min; give its 24-hour off time.

items.planAnswer: 1335 hours, because 4 h 50 min after 8:45 a.m. is 1:35 p.m., and 1:35 p.m. is 1335 hours

scoring.wrong: costs nothing, never marked, counted only for first try accuracy
scoring.stars: one for finishing, two at sixty per cent right first time, three at ninety; hidden with the first-try line by showScore false
scoring.phaseMount: a mount scores every phase it plays, from its phase to the last (+5 a question; phases of 3, 3, 3, 3 questions)
scoring.finishCard: stars and the Right first time line under the phase rows on the summary page

hostContract.phase: absent (not a finite number): the whole lesson, phases one to 4 in a row, the summary page at the end, finished once. Present: rounded and clamped to one to 4; the tool starts at that phase and, as the NCERT tools do, walks on by itself after each phase's last question (its closing line, then 1.4 s), in user and AI mode alike, through phase 4 to the summary page (a tool with nextKey, runtime r48+: in user mode it waits for the child's blinking Next key instead, after every question and every phase, and the last phase's key opens the summary; AI mode, and a host that mounts one phase without navigableDots, walk on by themselves); finished once, from the summary page.
hostContract.navigableDots: true (or no phase): user mode, the phase dots are controls; otherwise AI mode, the dots show progress and the agent drives window.toolApi.
